cells: GETTING UNSTUCK  |  A short, optional way forward when the IA stalls
An unobtrusive 'I'm stuck' link should be available throughout Completing. The help panel never interrupts the student or blocks saving their draft.
Choose the CURRENT problem; show one immediate action and at most two more possibilities. The student can choose Other, Not sure, Save or Return to where they were.
Practical barriers (late data, permissions, equipment or response delays) are reasons to adjust the PROJECT PLAN—not generic mathematical limitations to write in the IA.
Never manufacture a result, say a prediction was proved, imply consent has been obtained, or silently switch an aim/method/dataset. Keep original plan and the real status of data.

Original data unavailable? Students can still write a concise introduction, record tentative predictions and WHY, define terms, compare collection methods, research secondary sources, and plan the next purposeful maths.
Use existing aim, genuine motivation and who benefits; edit if needed.
Student writes own prose; no results or graph claims.
Only if intro is unfinished or worth revisiting.
A brief introduction does not require collected data.
What pattern/result do you think might occur, why, and what would it mean to the beneficiary IF true?
Tentative prediction with Not sure option; never prefill it as a finding.
Only when useful or missing, not compulsory for theoretical route.
Preserve first expectation if prediction later changes.
List intended variables, units, target population or model parameters; define unfamiliar terms before first use.
Short planning notes, not a mandatory glossary or completed analysis.
Planned variable names, units, sampling context
Match statistical, modelling or theory route.
Meaningful symbols; not generic x/y by default.
Compare sampling versus census where relevant, measurement methods, sources and permissions; why chosen for this aim?
Planned alternatives + rationale labelled PLAN, not executed methods.
Only route-relevant methods; no unstarted PMCC warnings.
Look for public official tables, research datasets, reputable institutional sources or published measurements.
Candidate link/citation and variables; source NOT yet verified until checked.
Offer search strategy only; no claims of automatic retrieval.
Secondary sources require provenance, comparability and citation.
Try a different permitted data collection approach
Could a smaller legitimate group, alternative measurement, approved school dataset or different time interval answer the question?
One possible method with scope/permission check.
Never suggest evading permission or sampling secretly.
Targeted feasible scope may change what can be concluded.
Make a PROVISIONAL plan for first representation
What first figure or calculation might reveal a meaningful question, when real evidence exists?
Planned representation, not a generated chart or observed pattern.
Aim, prediction and anticipated evidence type
Don't pretend planned data exist; graph isn't required.
A small abstract example must be labelled illustrative.
Consider a small legitimate theoretical case
Could a purely mathematical example clarify your question while empirical data are pending?
Hypothetical/symbolic case clearly labelled, or skip.
Only if mathematically worthwhile and teacher-appropriate.
Never fabricate measurements or treat illustration as validation.
Record who collected existing published data, their definitions, date and how source can be cited.
Short citation and data-source candidate status.
Secondary or published source if actually found
No invented references or assumed sampling design.
Check original provenance before comparing sources.
Review or narrow the original aim if evidence cannot be found
Could a feasible question using real accessible data still be meaningful to the intended beneficiary?
Optional transparent aim/method edit; teacher question if substantial.
Keep first aim and prediction history; no automatic changes.
Revisit whether actual maths still suits AI SL/AA SL.
Record ONE useful action and save
Choose a small next task now; can return to data later.
Short action, status Pending, optional time/date entered by student.
No assumed deadline or background reminder.
Allow Save at any point without claiming a draft is finished.
Distinguish what is already available from what is missing
What actual observations have you got? Are they suitable for limited descriptive work?
Record obtained vs awaiting, with quality and scope.
Real data and remaining source tasks
Never add dummy observations to reach a target n.
Substantiate which population any conclusion could apply to.
ALTERNATIVE DATA SOURCES  |  Matching the original aim matters more than simply finding numbers
Official statistics, public research tables or reputable educational/research repositories with the right variables.
Compare population, year, definitions, units, collection method, response patterns and selection.
Record source citation and whether same aim still holds.
Student must verify source; not an automatic data download.
Useful only if maths can answer the real aim.
Accessible class, club or smaller target group ONLY where consent/procedures permit.
Define sampled population; random vs convenience vs census honestly, sample sizes and bias.
Explain limited inference or revise audience/aim if necessary.
Do not treat a club sample as whole-school evidence.
No covert data collection or personal data uploads.
Could school-level, region-level or published summary statistics answer a revised question?
Check whether each record is an individual or an aggregate and what comparisons remain valid.
Adapt interpretation and avoid individual-level claims from group averages.
Do not mix aggregate and individual records as if equivalent.
Is there a defensible descriptive analysis of this group, even if wider inference isn't justified?
Count actual responses, missingness and group imbalance; avoid asserting sample representative.
Narrow aims/scope and identify mathematical consequences.
Never invent respondents or assume low response is harmless.
Teachers advise if project depth at risk.
Published parameter values or experimental data
Can reputable existing measurements inform or validate the proposed model?
Check physical definitions, time interval, measurement units, accuracy, context and source.
Use provenance; distinguish calibration from independent validation.
Don't label a literature value as a measurement personally taken.
Model validity depends on relevant input domain.
Could a smaller safe experiment or different measurable quantity answer the modelling question?
Check assumptions, limitations of range/resolution and actual feasibility.
Revise method transparently and keep underlying mathematical objective.
No unsafe experiments or unapproved subject measurements.
Avoid an experiment that yields only trivial maths.
Purely mathematical case or proof route
Does the investigation meaningfully proceed from definitions, algebra or a conjecture without empirical data?
Separate mathematical example from empirical validation; check course level with teacher.
Continue theoretical mathematics if it genuinely addresses the aim.
Do not pretend hypothetical values constitute measured evidence.
Teacher check if changing route substantially.
Could the provider share an accessible extract or published summary, when authorised?
Check that the extract has original sampling/definitions and enough detail for planned comparisons.
Make one reasonable follow-up; work on safe sections while waiting.
No pressure on respondents, access control bypass or inferred consent.
Missing data remains Pending until received.
Same topic, different date or population
Would a different period, age group, region or organisation still make the investigation meaningful?
Compare variable definitions, seasonality, context, population and representativeness.
Student may refine aim/beneficiary/prediction with reason.
Don't silently equate sources across incompatible periods/groups.
Preserve original expectation and audit changes.
Dataset looks available but cannot be used
Source may be behind a paywall, prohibited, incomplete or personally identifiable.
Check legal permission, privacy, provenance and alternative public route.
Record inaccessible / pending / unsuitable and next action.
Don't scrape around restrictions or upload sensitive details.
A listed URL doesn't mean data are usable.
Could carefully harmonised data provide meaningful comparisons?
Check consistent variable definitions, units, inclusion criteria, populations, missingness and source dates.
Keep full provenance and state consequences for interpretation.
Do not join mismatched columns or manipulate exclusions to produce desired pattern.
Prefer one coherent source when possible.
OTHER COMMON HICCOUGHS  |  Offer one useful route, not an overwhelming troubleshooting tree
Can I draft my introduction or prediction, or research a legitimate alternative source?
No real data required for a concise introduction or tentative prediction.
No fake results, graphs or conclusions.
Write intro / source shortlist / Not sure
What does my actual sample allow me to describe honestly?
Check representativeness/response bias and consider one feasible source change.
Don't assert full population claims or make up answers.
What safe preparatory work can I do before collecting anything?
Draft aim, intro, method alternatives and definitions; seek approval.
Never proceed with restricted collection before permission.
Secondary data don't match my original variables
Does this source still test the same claim with compatible definitions and units?
Look for compatible source or transparently refine aim and beneficiary.
No mismatched datasets passed off as equivalent.
Can I check original records, units and the actual effect of missing values?
Correct defensible errors, state exclusions and limits, possibly seek more genuine data.
No invented missing numbers or unexplained exclusions.
I have no idea how to begin writing
Can I start with one sentence explaining what I want to find out and why?
Use/edit planning aim, motivation and whom result might help; stay under a page.
I don't know what to predict
What do I suspect and WHY? Or is 'Not sure yet' more honest?
Optional plausible conjecture; if true what would it mean for beneficiary?
Do not force a correlation, fabricated prior belief or fake data.
What exactly looks different, and which mathematical check might explain it?
Describe actual result and consider a justified alternative/another angle.
Don't erase prediction or force data to fit.
My graph doesn't tell me much
What new insight would it give a reader? Would a short calculation be better?
Choose purposeful first move or omit repetitive graph.
No decorative graphs or compulsory figures.
I can't decide on the next maths
What question follows from what I actually observed?
Request one or two course-appropriate ideas, teacher question if beyond level.
No arbitrary sequence or unstarted technique limitations.
Do I understand enough to explain it, or could another method answer my aim better?
Focus on a justified in-course route and consult teacher if necessary.
Advanced maths for its own sake doesn't ensure quality.
The calculator or software isn't working
Can a simpler taught method or a different supported tool carry out the SAME mathematical task?
Keep inputs, goals and interpretation clear; use technology guidance only for actual output.
Don't invent results or substitute screenshot for understanding.
What did I calculate and what does it mean for my original aim?
Brief interpretation near actual result and defined symbols/accuracy.
No routine textbook derivation or long generic evaluation.
I have too much material and can't see a story
Which few figures/calculations actually help answer the aim?
Revisit aim, remove repetition, order results logically with reflections.
Don't save all evaluation for conclusion.
I am behind or draft feedback is overwhelming
What one concrete action matters most for the next school milestone?
Check actual date, teacher feedback permissions and choose small action.
No made-up deadlines, second written-feedback promise or automatic reminder.
I can't resume from a saved document
Was it a Pathfinder-generated file? What values can I recover manually?
Try permitted PDF/DOCX import or enter aim/prediction/source fields; keep current work.
Import is design spec only; never claim file parser exists now.
OPTIONAL SECONDARY SOURCE CHECK  |  Short, relevant and never a compulsory generic form
Check only when considering an alternative source
What a good answer looks like
Does the candidate source actually measure the quantities needed for the aim?
Definitions/units and observation level match; if not, what question can it support?
Source variable names, meaning, units and target comparison.
Does the dataset cover the intended population/place/time?
If not, limit conclusions or revise aim explicitly with student choice.
Population, time period, selection method and coverage.
Is the source trustworthy and traceable?
Record original organisation, date, link/DOI/publication, licence and method if published.
A real, attributable source; not 'I found a spreadsheet'.
Can you explain how the source values were collected?
Consider measurement accuracy, sampling/aggregation and missingness relevant to the mathematics.
Source metadata or clear 'Not stated' if unavailable.
Does the new source still answer something useful for the intended beneficiary?
If not, offer an honest revised aim or other source, not a forced calculation.
Current beneficiary/intended use and real data readiness.
Is access/consent/licence compatible with appropriate use?
Avoid private, identifiable and restricted data. Teacher approval isn't inferred.
Permission status; source use restrictions as needed.
Do you have the data now or just a candidate link?
Separate Candidate / Accessible / Checked / Used from Pending / Unavailable.
Explicit status, selected action and source citation.
What ONE feasible next step would allow meaningful maths?
Pick source check, collect authorised data, write introduction or save.
Student choice; no mandatory timeline or background monitoring.
STUDENT JOURNEY TESTS  |  These are acceptance criteria for the future website; not yet executed in a browser
No data access and intro missing
Show Write introduction / prediction / define terms / find secondary data and Save.
No graph or numerical analysis inferred from hypothetical values.
No data yet but prediction supplied
Prefill existing tentative prediction/WHY with Edit or Skip.
Never label original prediction as result.
Permit safe text drafting while showing unresolved permission.
No survey/measurement action suggested until authorised.
Suggest source discovery and source-fit checklist, not just 'download data'.
No claim that unrelated available dataset answers current aim.
Switching from primary to secondary source
Require student-confirmed source/aim/method review; keep historical plan.
No silent method switch or fabricated personal collection.
Only five responses when population much larger
Explain restricted scope/response uncertainty; student may consult teacher.
No spurious population inference or fake extra observations.
Prompt variable definition/units/population compatibility or reject source.
I don't understand the next maths
Show a relevant existing maths guide, not all options.
No unsolicited long help or calculator-generated result.
Return to exact stage/draft without losing entered text.
No mandatory completion of Help form.
Snapshot preserves issue category, action, source candidate and return stage.
Project is theoretical with no empirical data
Skip sample/census issues and suggest appropriate mathematical cases/teacher guidance.
No forced data collection or fake measurements.
Student has a broken document upload
Offer best-effort extraction/manual resume and Save; keep existing draft.
No claim PDF/DOCX import currently implemented.

DESIGN RULE: The normal experience has a small 'I'm stuck' action, not a separate compulsory worksheet. Persist current section, issue, ONE next task and source changes. Do not make the problem look like a marking weakness.
